d.g: A South Asian female servant, maid or nanny, historically, often one working for Europeans in South Asia.
d.x: She manufactured the Station scandal, and talked to her ayah.

ayah.e: From various Indian languages (e.g. Hindi आया (āyā, “dry nurse, nanny”)), from Portuguese aia (“nurse, governess”), from Latin avia (“grandmother”).

d.g: Ayapana triplinervis (syn. Eupatorium ayapana), a tropical American shrub

ayatollah.e: Borrowed from Iranian Persian آیَتُاللّٰه (âyato-l-lâh), from Classical Persian آیَةُاللّٰه (āyatu-l-lāh), from Arabic آيَةُ ٱللَّٰهِ (ʔāyatu llāhi, “sign of God”, from آيَة (ʔāya, “sign”) + اللّٰه (allāh, “God”)).

d.g: The sixteenth letter of many Semitic alphabets/abjads (Phoenician, Aramaic, Hebrew, Syriac, Arabic and others).
d.x: Ayin is the most difficult of the faucals.

ayin.e: From Proto-Semitic *ʿayn- (“eye”), particularly via Hebrew עַיִן (ʿáyin).

d.g: Alternative spelling of air (especially when referring to the form of music).

ayr.e: Borrowed from Manx ayr. Doublet of faeder, father, padre, pater, and père.

d.g: hardy breed of dairy cattle from Ayr, Scotland
(Sanskrit) an ancient medical treatise summarizing the Hindu art of healing and prolonging life;  sometimes regarded as a 5th Veda
